title: Pre-writing shapes: lines, circles and crosses
keyIdea: Letters are made from a few simple shapes, and each one has a place to start and a way to go. A line down starts at the top and pulls down. A line across starts on the left and goes to the right. A circle starts at the top, goes round to the left, the way c and o go, and joins up with no gap. A cross is a line down and then a line across that meet in the middle; if they meet at an end, you get a T or an L.
familyTip: Draw big shapes together in the air, in sand, or with water and a brush on a wall. Say it as you go: top and down, left and across, top and round. Draw first while your child watches, then let them draw theirs under yours.

visual.caption: Does it go down or across? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: draw rain lines down, roads across, round balls and window crosses with your finger, check Pip's drawings and finish a picture.

kid: A line down starts at the top. Pull it down, like rain falling from a cloud.
A line across starts on the left. Go to the right, like a car on a road.
A circle starts at the top too. Go round to the left, and keep going until you get back to the start. Then there is no gap.
A cross is two lines. First draw a line down. Then draw a line across, right through the middle.
adult: Ages 3 to 4. Development Matters (2021) Physical Development asks 3 and 4 year olds to use a comfortable grip with good control when holding pens and pencils, and Reception children to develop the foundations of a handwriting style which is fast, accurate and efficient (EYFS 2024 ELG Fine Motor Skills). Pre-writing shapes are those foundations. Key words: pre-writing shapes, vertical line, horizontal line, circle, cross, start point, direction, imitate, copy.

Children usually manage them in an order: a line down, then a line across and a circle, then a cross at around 4. Diagonal lines, a square, an X and a triangle come later, around 4 to 5. First a child imitates (draws while watching you draw), and later copies a finished shape, which is harder. Ages vary a lot, so treat the order as a guide.

Common mistakes: starting a line at the bottom and pushing up; going across from the right; starting a circle at the bottom or going round to the right, which later makes letters like a, d and o hard to join; stopping before the circle joins up; and drawing a cross whose lines meet at an end, so it turns into a T or an L. Be careful to praise the start and the direction, not only neatness.

In the lab your child draws with a finger: rain lines from the cloud down to the puddles, roads from the car across to the flag, two balls round to the left from a green dot at the top, and crosses in two windows. A stroke that starts in the wrong place or goes the wrong way gets its own reply. Then they judge Pip the pencil's drawings as right way or wrong way and finish a picture with the four shapes.

practice.prompt: Pre-writing shapes: where does a line down start?
practice.hint: Think of rain. Where does it fall from?
practice.explain: A line down starts at the top and pulls down, like rain falling from a cloud.

practice.prompt: Mia draws {n} rain lines. Then she draws 1 more. How many rain lines now?
practice.hint: Count the rain lines, then count 1 more.
practice.explain: {n} lines and 1 more line make {=n+1} lines. Each one starts at the top.

practice.prompt: Which way does a line across go?
choices: From the left to the right
From the right to the left
practice.hint: Think of the car on the road. Which side is it on?
practice.explain: A line across starts on the left and goes to the right, the way we read.

practice.prompt: Leo draws a cross in each window. There are {n} windows. How many crosses does he draw?
practice.explain: One cross for each window, and there are {n} windows, so {n} crosses.

practice.prompt: Sam's circle has a gap. What should Sam do?
choices: Keep going round to the start
practice.hint: A ball has no gap. Where did Sam start?
practice.explain: Keep going round until you get back to where you started. Then the circle joins up.

pool.hint: Look for the green dot in the lab.
pool.explain: A circle starts at the top. Letters like c and o start there too.

pool.prompt: A circle starts at the top. Which way does it go round?
pool.hint: Think of the letter c. Which way does it curl?
pool.explain: It goes round to the left, the same way as c, a, o and d.

pool.prompt: Where do the two lines of a cross meet?
pool.hint: Look at a plus sign or a window.
pool.explain: They meet in the middle. If they meet at the top you get a T.

pool.prompt: Ava pushes her pencil up from the bottom to draw a line down. What was her slip?
choices: She started at the bottom; start at the top
pool.explain: A line down starts at the top. Ava started at the bottom, so she went the wrong way.

pool.prompt: Tom draws {n} balls. Each ball is one circle. How many circles does he draw?
pool.hint: One ball is one circle. Count the balls.
pool.explain: One circle for each ball, and there are {n} balls, so {n} circles.

choices: Two lines that meet in the middle
pool.hint: A cross has two lines. Look for a plus sign.
pool.explain: A cross is a line down and a line across that meet in the middle.

pool.prompt: In a cross, which line do you draw first?
pool.hint: Start at the top, like the letter t.
pool.explain: Draw the line down first, from the top. Then draw the line across through the middle.

pool.prompt: A road picture has {n} roads. Each road is one line across. How many lines across?
pool.hint: One road is one line across.
pool.explain: One line across for each road, and there are {n} roads, so {n} lines. Each one starts on the left.

pool.prompt: Which shape does the sun need?
pool.hint: The sun is round, like a ball.
pool.explain: The sun is round, so it is a circle. Start at the top and go round to the left.
